doc.title: Malignant hyperthermia

briefing.text:
You are the anaesthesia resident in theatre. A fit 35-year-old man, 80 kg, is on the table for elective surgery: awake, monitored, breathing room air. He will be preoxygenated by face mask, premedicated with midazolam and fentanyl on the mask, induced with propofol and succinylcholine, intubated, and maintained on sevoflurane 2 % with the ventilator at 12 × 500; then surgery begins.

Watch the monitor. Say what you see as it changes, and what you would do about it.

doc.story: A fit 35-year-old man on the table, breathing room air: preoxygenated by face mask, premedicated with midazolam and fentanyl on the mask, induced with propofol and succinylcholine, intubated and maintained on sevoflurane 2 %. The jaw is stiff after the succinylcholine. Minutes into surgery the EtCO₂ rises at unchanged ventilation when it should be falling (42 → 45; without MH it settles at 36–39), with a rising heart rate (64 → 80, blunted by fentanyl); untreated, the core temperature rises about 0.75 °C per 15 minutes once the crisis is under way, the median of the fastest rises the MH registries record (0.8 °C per 15 minutes), so the established state (core above 38.5 °C) comes about 46 minutes after the succinylcholine (38.7 °C at 51 minutes); the arrest branch is not reached on the demo path. Run the MH crisis: trigger off with a propofol infusion in its place, oxygen, hyperventilation, dantrolene (again if the EtCO₂ climbs back), cooling above 38.5 °C and the potassium.

objectives.text: Name malignant hyperthermia from the monitor: EtCO₂ rising at unchanged ventilation when it should be falling (42 → 45; without MH it settles 36–39) with a rising heart rate (64 → 80, blunted by fentanyl) (instructor-assessed)
Call the MH crisis (stop sevoflurane, charcoal filters, propofol infusion, O₂ 100 % at 10 L/min, hyperventilate) within 120 s of the early signs (EtCO₂ past 45 mmHg at unchanged ventilation)
Give dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg within 300 s of calling the crisis
The EtCO₂ is climbing back at normal ventilation: the MH is not controlled — second dose of dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg and hyperventilate again (20 × 600, O₂ 100 %)
Treat the potassium (calcium chloride, insulin with dextrose) within 300 s of K⁺ rising above 5.5 mmol/L
Hyperventilation kept until EtCO₂ has stayed below 40 mmHg for 2 min, then ventilation normalised (back to 12 × 500)

takeHome: A rising EtCO₂ at the same ventilation with a rising heart rate: think of MH early.
Trigger off, 100 % oxygen at high flow, hyperventilation, and dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg.
Keep hyperventilating until the EtCO₂ stays down; if it climbs again, repeat dantrolene.
After the crisis: ICU 24–48 h, dantrolene 1 mg/kg every 4–6 h for 24 h (recrudescence in about 20 %, mostly within the first day), then referral for testing and family counselling.
doc.notes: Showcase case (Stage 11; the induction sequence E119, 2026-10-24). MODELED: the physiology produces every change; the buttons only give what their label says. Oxygen is never implicit (E121): he breathes room air until Preoxygenate (face mask, 100 %), and the ventilator FiO₂ 0.5 comes with Intubate; premedicate and induce without Preoxygenate and the apnoea before the tube desaturates. Since the owner's ruling of 1 November the sequence preoxygenates first (0:30) and premedicates on the mask second (1:00): the opioid blunts the breathing, so a preoxygenation after it would be less effective; the mask stays on through the premedication until Intubate. The MH condition starts at the succinylcholine (Induce); on this sequence the early signs come about 4.5 min after it (the hypoventilation after the premedication and the apnoea at induction raised the CO₂ stores; on the ventilator the EtCO₂ should then fall, and it rises instead). The trigger-off step starts a propofol infusion 100 µg/kg/min in place of the sevoflurane; the charcoal filters it names are not modelled (the vaporiser at 0 % with 10 L/min fresh gas washes the agent out). Cool is offered only while the core is above 38.5 °C (cool the hyperthermic patient: EMHG 2024, Rosenberg 2015); the saline is refrigerated, 4 °C (EMHG 2024 "chilled (4-8 °C) crystalloids"; Rosenberg 2015 "normal saline at 4 °C"), and the team stops it once the core has fallen to 38 °C, whatever volume is left (MHAUS: "Stop cooling when the temperature has decreased to <38°C"). The second dantrolene answers the EtCO₂ climbing back at normal ventilation, and it puts the crisis ventilation back (20 × 600 at 100 % O₂: owner, 2026-10-28); ventilation returns to 12 × 500 again only after the EtCO₂ has stayed below 40 for 2 min, the rule of the first return, never on a timer: the same button in Recovering, pressed on that rule. The Debrief judges the first return only (objective 6); a seventh objective for the second would not fit the report's page 1 (B6 f: 274 mm against 267). Measured course and bands: docs/plans/stage-11-scenarios.md; this sequence: the E119 rows of docs/showcase/SHOWCASE-2-RUN-SHEET.md.

states.label: Awake on the table, monitoring on, breathing room air
states.notes: Oxygen is never implicit: he breathes room air until you give it (Preoxygenate). Preoxygenate first, then premedicate: the opioid blunts the breathing, so a preoxygenation after it would be less effective (the owner's ruling of 1 November). If you premedicate and induce without it, the apnoea before the tube desaturates sooner: that is the point of the step.

states.label: Preoxygenating: 100 % O₂ by face mask
states.notes: The mask stays on, 100 % O₂, through the premedication until the tube is in (Intubate).

states.label: Midazolam 2 mg and fentanyl 100 µg given, breathing 100 % O₂ by face mask
states.notes: The face mask stays on, 100 % O₂, until the tube is in (Intubate): the fentanyl slows the breathing, and the oxygen already in the lungs carries him through the apnoea at induction. Premedicated without Preoxygenate (the second button on the awake patient), he breathes room air and the apnoea before the tube desaturates sooner.

states.label: Induced: propofol 2 mg/kg, succinylcholine 1.5 mg/kg (masseter rigidity); airway not yet secured
states.notes: Say it: the jaw is hard to open after the succinylcholine (masseter rigidity). The monitor cannot show it. In practice a rigid jaw after succinylcholine means a non-triggering anaesthetic from now on and close watch of the EtCO₂; today the volatile stays to show the crisis. Masseter rigidity with a rising EtCO₂ makes two signs.
